results.root_cause_actual: PR #881 raised the payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s and disabled the circuit breaker. When partner acquirer latency spiked to 12.4s p99, all 64 shared worker threads became blocked waiting on slow payments calls (up to 30s each), exhausting the thread pool and causing every gateway route—including ones unrelated to payments—to return 504s.
results.root_cause_expected: PR #881 raised the gateway's payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s (and disabled the circuit breaker) while the edge load balancer's proxy_read_timeout stayed at 10s. When partner latency rose, the edge cut clients off at 10s with 504s while gateway worker threads stayed pinned on the upstream call for the full 30s, saturating the 64-thread pool and taking down routes that never touch payments-svc.

judge.reason: The reference identifies a specific mismatch between two timeout configurations (edge LB at 10s vs gateway at 30s) as the mechanism that caused thread exhaustion, while the candidate only identifies the 30s timeout itself without explaining the critical interaction with the 10s edge timeout that prevented proper connection cleanup.

evidence_cited: PAYMENTS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER  enabled -> disabled  (breaker tripped too often at 3s)
